name: Apple MacBook Air 13 (M4)
description: A thin, fanless laptop that stays silent in lectures and lasts a full day away from a socket. The 256 GB of storage fills up quickly, so plan to keep big files in the cloud.

name: Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 15
description: A dependable everyday laptop for notes, research and online classes at a friendly price. Its 8 GB of memory handles documents and browsing, but many open apps will slow it down.

name: ASUS TUF Gaming A15
description: A tough gaming laptop with an RTX 4060 graphics card that also runs 3D modelling and engineering software well. It is heavy and the battery is short, so it suits a desk more than a backpack.

name: HP Envy x360 14
description: A convertible laptop whose touch screen folds back into a tablet for handwritten notes and sketches. A good all-rounder for students who switch between typing and drawing.

name: ASUS Zenbook 14 OLED
description: A light 14-inch laptop with a sharp OLED screen and a full terabyte of storage. It is easy to carry all day and fast enough for programming and multitasking.

name: Acer Aspire 3
description: The lowest-cost laptop in the list, with a full-size keyboard and number pad for spreadsheets. It is fine for writing and browsing, but the 256 GB of storage is small.

name: Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x
description: One of the longest-lasting laptops in the list, thanks to an efficient Snapdragon processor. Most study apps run well, but check that any specialist Windows software you need supports Arm.

name: MSI Katana 15
description: A gaming laptop with an RTX 4060 card and a fast Core i7 for games, rendering and machine learning practice. Expect fan noise under load and well under half a day of battery.

name: Lenovo Yoga Pro 9i 16
description: A large-screen creator laptop with a bright mini-LED display and an RTX 4060 for video editing and 3D work. It has plenty of memory, but at 2.1 kg it is a lot to carry.

name: Microsoft Surface Pro 11
description: A tablet with a detachable keyboard, light enough to carry everywhere and great with a pen for notes. The keyboard and pen cost extra, and the 256 GB of storage is limited.

name: HP 15
description: A plain, practical 15.6-inch laptop with a Core i5 processor for assignments and video calls. A sensible pick if you want a big screen on a small budget.

name: HP OmniBook X 14
description: A slim laptop with a Snapdragon processor, a terabyte of storage and close to a full day of battery. A strong choice for writing, research and coding on the go.

name: Lenovo LOQ 15
description: The most affordable gaming laptop in the list, with an RTX 4050 graphics card for games and GPU coursework. It is bulky, so it is better as a desk machine than a daily carry.

name: Apple MacBook Pro 14 (M4)
description: A powerful 14-inch laptop with a very bright screen and the longest battery life in the list. It costs a lot, but it handles video, design and development work for years.

name: Dell Inspiron 14 2-in-1
description: A budget-friendly convertible with a touch screen that folds into tent and tablet modes. The 8 GB of memory is the main limit if you keep many apps open.

name: ASUS Vivobook Go 15
description: A low-cost laptop for typing, browsing and online lectures. It is not built for heavy software, but it does the basics well.

name: Acer Swift Go 14
description: A light, well-built 14-inch laptop with a Core Ultra processor and a sharp screen. It balances price, weight and speed well for most degrees.

name: HP Victus 16
description: A 16-inch gaming laptop with an RTX 4060 and a terabyte of storage for games and large projects. The big screen is comfortable for long sessions, but the laptop is heavy.

name: Acer Swift X 14
description: A compact creator laptop with an OLED screen and an RTX 4050 card for photo and video editing. It is lighter than most laptops with a graphics card.

name: Lenovo Yoga 7i 2-in-1 14
description: A convertible laptop with a 360-degree hinge and a touch screen for notes and presentations. Its efficient processor gives it a long battery life for the price.

name: Dell Inspiron 15 3530
description: A budget laptop with 16 GB of memory, so it copes with more open tabs and apps than most in its price range. A solid choice for programming courses.

name: ASUS ROG Strix G16
description: The most powerful gaming laptop in the list, with a Core i9 and an RTX 4070 for demanding games and simulations. It is expensive, heavy and short on battery life.

name: ASUS ProArt P16
description: A premium creator laptop with an OLED touch screen, 32 GB of memory and an RTX 4060 for video, 3D and AI work. It is the most expensive laptop in the list.

name: Samsung Galaxy Book4 Pro 360
description: A large 16-inch convertible with an AMOLED touch screen and an included pen. It is thin for its size, but the big screen makes it heavier than smaller 2-in-1 laptops.
